text:
jon_customer: Hey team — our production job started failing after we bumped to the new embeddings API. Getting a dimension mismatch and a bunch of timeouts when we send batched requests. Impact: search index pipeline stalled, ~30% of batches failing. Anyone seen this?

alex_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact error and a minimal repro? Also which model + SDK version are you on?

jon_customer: Error is this (from our Python worker logs):
```
ValueError: embedding dimensionality mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024
  at embeddings_endpoint.py:42
```
We're calling model "text-embed-legacy-2" via python-sdk v1.4.2. Code simplified:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=...)
texts = ["doc1", "doc2", ...]  # batches of ~128
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embed-legacy-2", input=texts)
```
Sometimes it works for small batches but fails for large ones; also we see intermittent HTTP 504/timeouts when we set batch size to 256.

alex_support: Ok — first checks: 1) confirm the model's embedding dimension in the model catalog (1536 vs 1024). 2) Are you mixing calls to different models (old+new) in the same worker process / reuse of client? 3) any custom post-processing that reshapes vectors?

maria_sdk: pinging here — there was a bug in python-sdk 1.4.2 batching logic where if a user passed a flat list vs list-of-strings it could reorder and cause truncated inputs, sometimes causing the service to route to a fallback model with different dim. Also retry/timeout defaults were aggressive. Can you show how you build 'texts' and any custom retry wrappers?

jon_customer: we do: `texts = sum(chunks, [])` — naive flatten from our side. here's the chunk generator and call:
```python
def chunks(it, n):
    for i in range(0, len(it), n):
        yield it[i:i+n]

for c in chunks(all_docs, 128):
    resp = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embed-legacy-2", input=c, timeout=30)
```
No custom retry, just rely on sdk.

nisha_ml: quick model note: newer open models (and some Redwood variants) have 1536 vs 1024 dims. If a fallback to a different model variant occurs (routing policy), you'll see the mismatch when we try to bulk index into a vector store that expects a fixed size. But rippling timeouts point to batching/throughput issues too.

sam_infra: FYI infra metrics show bursts of "request split" events when payload > ~200KB — we throttle and split large batch payloads across multiple backend workers. There was a regression in request combiner that changed how batch boundaries are honored for some SDK payload shapes — that could explain reorders.

alex_support: Can you run a quick single-item call for a sample doc and print len(embedding) returned? Also try forcing batch_size=1 to see if errors stop.

jon_customer: single-call returns length 1536. When I do batch of 128 we fail ~40% of time with the dimension mismatch. When successful, the shapes are all 1536. Output from failing batch contains some vectors of length 1024 (weird).

maria_sdk: Thanks — that's consistent with a bug we've tracked (SDK-embed-batch-reorder). Workaround: downgrade to python-sdk 1.4.0 or apply this client-side check before indexing: verify len(vec) == expected_dim and skip+log if not. We'll ship a patch in 1.4.3. For timeout + throughput: set `timeout=90` or use the SDK's `max_batch_size` config to limit per-request payload instead of trying huge batches.

alex_support: Repro steps for us: 1) provide a failing payload (you can DM a small snippet) 2) confirm whether you reuse client across threads/processes; 3) try the downgrade/workaround.

jon_customer: DMed a sanitized payload (100 items). Also we do reuse a global client across worker threads in a multiprocessing pool.

maria_sdk: Reusing client across processes is unsupported in current runtime — you should instantiate client per process or use the new `Client.for_worker()` helper in 1.4.3. Reuse across forked processes can corrupt batching state. If you're using gunicorn with preload, that can cause this.

sam_infra: Additionally, for the timeouts: our backend splits big batches which can cause longer tail latency for last shards. If you need lower p95, aim for smaller per-batch sizes (<=64) or enable concurrent smaller requests and let the platform batch. We can also increase per-customer concurrency temporarily; need a support request id.

jon_customer: Ok will try instantiate per worker and reduce to 64. Quick question on retry: what's recommended pattern for idempotency? If a partial batch fails (some vectors returned), do you retry whole batch?

nisha_ml: Best practice: make each unit-of-work idempotent at doc level. Do per-document retries with exponential backoff. For embeddings, safer to request per-doc or small batches and dedupe by doc id on ingest. If you must retry full batch, validate vector dims before overwriting index.

maria_sdk: We're releasing 1.4.3 with: fix for batch reorder, improved retry logic (binary exponential backoff with jitter), increased default timeout to 60s, and a `validate_embeddings=True` flag that will surface dimension mismatches in the SDK before returning results. Patch ETA: 3 hours.

deploy-bot: deploy status: sdk/python 1.4.3 patch build passed unit tests, staging deploy in 15m.

alex_support: I'll keep an eye on infra for any bucketed errors. Jon, please try these steps and report back. If still failing we'll open a support case to bump infra limits and capture tcpdumps.

jon_customer: Tried per-process client + batch_size=64 + upgraded to 1.4.3 pre-release. So far stable for ~3 hours, failures dropped to 0. No more dimension mismatch. Throughput is slightly lower but acceptable. Thanks!! :tada:

alex_support: Awesome — closing loop: we'll follow up with a summary doc and the SDK release notes pointing to the `Client.for_worker()` usage and batching guidance. If you want, we can also schedule a call to walk through ingest pipeline optimizations.

jon_customer: Happy to do a short call. Thanks all.

maria_sdk: Filed SDK-1234 to track permanent fix + docs. Adding sample snippet for recommended usage:
```python
# per-worker client
from redwood import Client
client = Client.for_worker(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
# small batches + validate
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embed-legacy-2", input=batch, validate_embeddings=True, timeout=90)
```

alex_support: Marking thread resolved for now. If anything pops up, reopen. :white_check_mark:
